sourceContext: // A fixed secondary must not replace an unknown callback or expose provider details.
reason: SS343 handoff must attempt reacquisition/readiness of the original advisory lock in finally after the borrowed callback. Known restoration failure emits fixed Failure only without an unknown callback; otherwise it attaches a fresh fixed secondary and preserves the outgoing unknown callback. Silencing this finally failure could claim a restored parent ownership state without evidence. Actual handoff/lock/DB proof is separate and not executed.

SS332/341/343 owned JDBC close is attempted directly in the explicit finally. Conditional replacement follows the declared known-SQL versus unknown Runtime/Error primary/secondary matrix; it may deliberately let an unknown cleanup escape instead of known SQL or an absent primary. Otherwise the exact outgoing primary and safe suppression remain. Removing a finally throw or mechanically applying TWR would alter that matrix/cleanup uncertainty. The outer finally still attempts its own acquired resource; borrowed parent responsibility remains explicit.
